subject: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — review and acceptance
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@cedarbank.com>, security@cedarbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — review and acceptance

Hi Claire / Cedar Security team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is an updated network boundary diagram and the KMS interface spec that align with Cedar Bank's requirement to keep key material operations inside your VPC and to restrict remote key material egress.

Key points for review (high level):
- BYOK model: customer-supplied master keys (KMIP/HSM wrapped) stored in customer KMS. Redwood will be provided a wrapped/delegated key handle that we never unwrap in the hosted control plane.
- Crypto operations: model-serving HSM/KMS calls must originate from nodes inside your VPC (we propose a private peering lane). No plaintext key material leaves Cedar's environment.
- Egress constraints: outbound connections from Redwood-managed Pods to KMS endpoints are allowed only over dedicated VPC peering with explicit CIDR filters; we will not persist key material in our control plane logs.

Action items for Cedar to confirm:
1) Acceptance of proposed peering ranges (10.20.0.0/16 -> 10.30.0.0/16 in diagram).
2) Whether Cedar will run an HSM (on-prem) with KMIP or prefer a cloud-managed HSM with strict VPC endpoints.
3) Preferred rotation window and whether remote operator access should be allowed for emergency unseal (we default to operator split / no remote unseal).

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf, kms-interface-spec.xlsx.

I'll loop Tom from CloudBroker for the peering details once we have confirmation.

Thanks,
Rafael
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: network-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram, 1 page)
Attachment: kms-interface-spec.xlsx (spreadsheet, 6 sheets)
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@cedarbank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cedarbank.com, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cloudbroker.net>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:06:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — review and acceptance

Rafael,

Appreciate the summary and the artifacts. High level: Cedar is comfortable with the BYOK approach provided the following are enforced by contract and configuration:
- All KMIP/HSM calls must terminate inside our VPC and be routed over the dedicated peering. No fallbacks to public endpoints.
- Redwood must not request or store unwrapped key material at any stage; we need attestations for this.
- Any operator with unseal privileges must be Cedar-controlled (no Redwood operator with HSM key shares).

A few clarifying Qs:
1) Can Redwood provide an attestation report we can ingest (simple signed JSON) showing the runtime nodes that made KMS calls and confirmation they used the peered path?
2) For rotations: we want a weekly rolling-kek rotation window for the first 3 months to validate ops; afterwards monthly is OK.

Tom from CloudBroker should help with the peering ACLs and routing. If Redwood is comfortable with the conditions above we can move the DocuSign BYOK addendum to signature.

Claire
Head of Cloud Security — Cedar Bank
---
External comment: security@cedarbank.com requests auditor contact for SOC evidence
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — internal ops plan

Team,

Forwarding Claire's reply. Points I want to lock down before we ask for signature:

1) Runtime attestations: we can emit a signed audit envelope per rotation event. Ops can produce a compact attestation (signed timestamp, node-id, destination IP, TLS fingerprint). Engineering (Jordan) — can you confirm we can emit that from the agent running on the enclave and that the signing key never leaves the runtime? Need to confirm format for Cedar.

2) Peering and ACLs: CloudBroker will provision the VLAN/peering. We must limit egress to the specific KMS IPs and port 5696 (KMIP) / 443 (REST KMS). Proposed ACLs are in sheet 3 of kms-interface-spec.xlsx.

3) Rotation cadence: we can support weekly KEK wrap rotations for the first 3 months as Claire requested. Need to document impact on cache warmup and latency (we expect a small tokenization/cache miss spike for ~1–2 minutes per shard). I'll draft a short runbook for the weekend maintenance windows.

4) Operators: Redwood will not maintain unseal shares for Cedar. We will provide procedures for emergency operator-assisted remote-unseal that rely solely on Cedar-run key holders and an automated remote attestation handshake. Noted: no Redwood person will be granted unseal privileges.

Next steps: Jordan please reply with the attestation payload example and whether signed envelopes can be pushed into the Drive link. I'll assemble the one-pager for the DocuSign addendum.

-Kimberly
VP, Product Security — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — attestation payload example

Kim / team,

We can emit a compact attestation object from the runtime process. Example (we'll provide as a JSON file in the Drive, sample fields below):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- node_id: shard-12a
- cert_fingerprint: SHA256:AB:...
- dest_ip: 10.20.2.13
- kmi_operation: Encrypt/Sign
- rotation_event: kek-2027-03-09
- signature: base64(sig)

Notes:
- The signing key is an enclave-local key pair provisioned at runtime via the hardware root of trust; private key never leaves the node and is rotated on node restart.
- We will push signed attestations to the Cedar-shared Drive folder; they will be retained for 90 days by default (we can extend on request).
- For real-time verification Cedar's auditors can query our trace endpoint over the peered lane to retrieve attestation envelopes; this endpoint will only be reachable over the peering and with mutual TLS.

ACL specifics: We will accept CloudBroker's suggested ACLs. Per Claire's ask, we'll restrict outbound to the CIDR block 10.20.0.0/16 and port 5696/443; source port ephemeral.

I'll upload the sample attestation and a short runbook describing the weekly rotation sequence.

-Jordan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: sample-attestation-20270309.json (signed envelope)
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cloudbroker.net>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Claire Huang <claire.huang@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 15:43:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Tenant encryption boundary & KMS egress constraints — peering confirmed

Rafael / Claire,

CloudBroker has provisioned the peering and the ACLs per the spec. Summary:
- Peering: cedar-vpc-peer (10.20.0.0/16 -> 10.30.0.0/16), HA BGP session across two iBGP links.
- ACLs: outbound to 10.20.0.0/16 on 5696 and 443 only; ICMP allowed for path MTU; no NAT applied.
- MTU & path: jumbo frames disabled; no TCP MSS rewriting.

I've also uploaded the peering acceptance test steps to the shared Drive and initiated the first connectivity smoke test — results: OK (KMIP handshake succeeded from shard-12a, TLS cert matched expected fingerprint).

Claire — if you approve the DocuSign addendum I will trigger the final network cutover tomorrow morning.

Tom
Solutions Engineer — CloudBroker
